chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you encounter a predatory beast, recite Ayat al-Kursi in its face, and say to it: I impose upon you by the Determination of Allah, and the Determination of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and the Determination of Suleiman ibn Dawud (peace be upon him), and the Determination of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and the Pure Imams after him, for indeed it will turn away from you, if Allah wills.'

He said: So I went out, and behold the beast had presented itself. I imposed upon it and said to it: 'Unless you step aside from our path and do not harm us.' He said: So I looked at it, and it had bowed its head, and put its tail between its legs, and turned away.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.عَزَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ: I impose upon you / I determine against you (a form of invocation)

ai.seo_question: How to protect oneself from wild animals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia concept of *Azzamah* (solemn invocation), where the authority of the Imams is invoked alongside Allah to command creation, reflecting their role as intermediaries of divine power. The narrative emphasizes the efficacy of these spiritual tools in taming wild beasts, a common motif in Shia hagiography demonstrating the Imams' dominion over nature. It serves as both a practical supplication for travelers and a theological affirmation of the Imams' unique status in the cosmic hierarchy.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kahily who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you come across a predatory wild animal, so recite Ayat Al-Kursy [2:255] in its face, and say to it: ‘I am determined against you by the Determination of Allahazwj, and determination of Muhammadsaww, and determination of Suleyman Bin Dawoodas, and determination of Amir Al-Momineen Aliasws Bin Abu Talibasws and the Purified Imamsasws from after himasws’, so it would be exchanged from him, Allahazwj Willing.

So a wild animal presented itself, so I was determined against it and said it to it so it step aside from our way and did not harm us. So I looked at it and it had bowed its head and entered its tail between its legs and left’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahili who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whenever you may come face to face with a wild beast, read verse 255 of Chapter 2 of the Holy Quran to its face and say, “I swear you by the oath of Allah, the oath of Muhammad (a.s.) the oath of Solomon son of David, the oath of Amir al-Mu’Mini, Ali ibn abu Talib and A ’immah, the clean ones (of all sins), after the Holy Prophet.” The beast will turn away from you by the will of Allah.’

I (the narrator) went out and a wild beast came face to face with me. I then swore it and said to it to turn and move out of the way without harming me. I looked at the beast, who had bent his head down, with the tail between the two legs and turned away.’”
